content: The duration of our passions depends no more upon ourselves than does the duration of our lives.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
sourceWork: Memoirs of the Regency of Anne of Austria
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
